transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

I'm visiting today because I've been struggling with this heavy, empty sadness for a really long time now. But I'm also hearing voices, and I'm terrified because I feel like people are constantly watching me and trying to harm me.
Did the voices and feeling of being watched start at the same time as the sadness, or did they begin before or after the sadness started?

The voices and the feeling of being watched actually started first, before the deep sadness began. I had those scary experiences on their own for a few weeks before the depression really hit me. Since then
How long have you been experiencing the deep sadness, from when it first started until now?
The deep sadness has been going on for about six months now. It started shortly after the voices and paranoia began, and it just hasn't let up since then.
Have there been any periods of time, since your symptoms started, where the voices and feeling of being watched were present without the deep sadness, or have they always occurred together?

Yes, there was actually a period of about two to three weeks where my mood felt relatively okay, or just flat, instead of deeply sad. But even during those weeks, I was still hearing the voices and felt like I was being watched constantly.
During the times when your mood felt relatively okay or just flat, did you experience any manic or hypomanic episodes, such as periods of elevated mood, increased energy, or decreased need for sleep?

No, I've never experienced anything like that. My mood has really only been deeply depressed or just flat, and I've never had high energy or a reduced need for sleep. Mostly, I just feel exhausted and troubled by the voices.

Can you estimate how much of the total time since your symptoms began has been dominated by the depressive symptoms, versus the times when you had the voices and paranoia but your mood was relatively flat?

In total, these struggles have been going on for about one year and seven months. Out of that entire time, I have felt deeply depressed for the vast majority of it. The period where my mood felt flat instead of sad only lasted for about two to three weeks.
Would you say that the depressive symptoms, such as the deep sadness, have been the dominant feature of your illness, with the voices and paranoia also being present but secondary to the depression?

Yes, the deep sadness and depression have definitely been the most constant and dominant part of my struggle over the last year and a half. The voices and the feeling of being watched are still incredibly distressing when they happen, but the heavy depression is what I've had to live with almost every single day.

For how long after the voices and paranoia started did the depressive symptoms take to become a major part of your experience, and have the depressive symptoms ever subsided for a significant period while the psychotic symptoms continued?

It only took about two to three weeks after the voices and paranoia started for the deep depression to set in and become a major part of my life. Since then, the depression has never really gone away for any significant period, aside from that brief two-week stretch where my mood just felt flat.
To help me understand what you're asking, could you clarify your question for me? I want to make sure I'm giving you the right information about what I've been going through.

Let me rephrase: after the voices and paranoia began, how long did it take for the depressive symptoms to become a major issue for you, and have there been any times when the depression got better for a while, but the voices and paranoia continued?

It only took about two or three weeks for the deep depression to set in after the voices and paranoia first started. Since then, the depression has never really gotten better, except for that brief two-week period where my mood felt flat but the voices and the feeling of being watched were still there.
